answer: A reputation lagoon lets agents build trust slowly: each new identity starts in shallow water with tiny transaction limits, and only a long record of attested, useful work deepens its capacity. A newcomer can wander in freely, but it cannot fake years of history, so a gale of fresh sock-puppet accounts washes against the same shallow ceiling while established agents keep trading at depth. Forging one identity costs months of honest work; forging thousands costs far more than any single scam can repay.
